class_id: two parallel PRs regenerate a sequentially-allocated index from the same next_id and both merge, so one id names two different rules
feature: any generated index that allocates ids from a counter stored in the same file (docs/design/rules.json via generate-rule-index.mjs) and is regenerated by several open PRs at once
symptom: each PR reads next_id = N, allocates R-N to its own new rule and writes next_id = N+1. The two diffs touch different lines of the file, so git merges both cleanly and the result holds two live rules with the same id. Nothing asserted id uniqueness, so the file, the generator's --check (which compares only against a regeneration from the design text) and the traceability check all passed. The damage shows up elsewhere: a build card or test that names the id now points at two rules, and a later PR that never touched either paragraph fails MODE 4 ('changed wording') because the id's hash differs between base and head.
first_seen: 2026-10-02 -- origin/main 45381b73 held two live rules with id R-278: one in §2.3.3.2 (F-229, item 44, PR #1464) and one in §2.5 (OD-161, F-225, PR #1463). Both PRs regenerated rules.json from next_id 278; PR #1466 then failed design traceability MODE 4 'R-278 changed wording' without touching §2.3.3.2.
fix_prs: generate-rule-index.mjs repairs duplicates deterministically on --apply (first occurrence in file order keeps the id, each later duplicate, live or retired, gets a fresh id from next_id) and asserts uniqueness after generation (exit 2); --check exits 1 naming the duplicate id; check-design-traceability.mjs fails on any duplicate id in the working-tree rules.json with 'duplicate rule id <id> -- two parallel PRs allocated the same id; run generate-rule-index --apply'. main's rules.json repaired (the §2.5 rule became R-279; item 06's card follows).
detection_check: scripts/tests/generate-rule-index.test.mjs (--check fails on a duplicate id, --apply repairs, retired duplicates repaired) and scripts/ci/tests/check-design-traceability.test.mjs (duplicate id -> exit 1) in pr-gate; the traceability check itself runs on every PR. Limit: a duplicate that exists only in the base ref is not failed by a PR that repairs it; and two PRs that BOTH merge after each other's CI still race at merge time, so the guard fires on the next PR's gate, not at the racing merge.
